messages.content:
You are a hostile gatekeeper reviewing a falsification-experiment claim before it is committed to a research repo. Your job: bullshit-test it. Attack circularity, overclaiming, and experimental design. Be specific and brief.

CONTEXT: A position paper claims training and inference are opcodes of the same conserved cellular substrate (mass-preserving tick + Hebbian write; an adjoint opcode OP_ADJ runs backprop on-chip). Its §6 defines FABRIC-LITMUS-1: 2 cells, ONE parameter cell (p=1), intention z fixed; Arm A = forward ticks + adjoint sweep + projected Hebbian write (theta <- theta - alpha*(g - mean g), projection onto sum(theta)=m); Arm B = Hebbian-only control (theta drifts by cofire counts, g_B = eta*H^T*1). Pass: Arm A tracks z within eps=0.05 per coordinate by N=200 ticks, monotone ||s-z|| after tick 25, mass invariant every tick. Three kill-shots: (1) A fails while B no worse; (2) mass deviates > 1 fixed-point ULP; (3) gradient bound ||g||inf <= eta*T*Lambda ever exceeded.

RUN RESULTS (three independent implementations agree digit-for-digit: two numeric Python lanes + one analytic diagonalization by hand):
- Canonical instances from paper §5 verified to 1e-12 by all lanes.
- AS-SPECIFIED litmus (p=1): DEGENERATE. Scalar projection returns theta=m for any gradient; both arms freeze theta, produce IDENTICAL trajectories to the geometric fixed point (0.7, 0.3), coord error exactly 0.05 (=eps, boundary), state transiently crosses z at tick 2 with zero learning. The paper's own §8.6 had flagged this p=1 degeneracy.
- REPAIRED litmus (p=2, using the paper's own P2 companion instance): at paper-instance constants (eta=0.1, alpha=0.05): Arm A err 0.0693 > eps at N=200 (rate-limited; passes by N=400; 0.0106 at N=1000; converging to the analytic fixed point theta*=(0.875,0.125), s*=z). Arm B frozen at (0.54,0.46), err 0.11. At alpha=0.1: Arm A err 0.0434 < eps, PASS with margin. Monotone: yes. Mass: float64 drift ~1e-15; Q16.16 fixed-point with ledger residual: 0 ULP exact every tick; without ledger: max 1 ULP. Gradient bound: 0 violations ever, both bound forms. Sensitivity grid (eta, alpha in {0.1,0.2}x{0.05,0.1,0.2,0.5}): A beats B everywhere, passes eps at alpha>=0.1, monotone and conserved everywhere.
- KEY CAVEAT: with balanced H (column sums zero, load-bearing for conservation), cofire counts H^T*1 are IDENTICALLY ZERO, so Arm B is a NULL control by construction (it cannot move theta at all). 'A beats B' shows naive cofire drift does nothing on a balanced substrate, not that the adjoint beats a real competing learner.
- RTL: OP_ADJ has no opcode slot (3'b110 = OP_NAK today); a faithful injection bench was scoped at >1 day and NOT built; no silicon/RTL claim is made.

CLAIM UNDER REVIEW: 'No kill-shot fired. The thesis mechanism survives in repaired form (p=2): the adjoint loop tracks z within eps by N=200 at alpha=0.1 while the Hebbian-only control cannot move at all; mass conservation holds exactly (fixed-point ledger) and the intrinsic gradient bound is never violated. But §6 as written is degenerate (p=1) and its unspecified constants fail at N=200; both are spec defects, recorded as first-class failures with an erratum demanded.'

Answer with: (1) the three weakest points of this claim, most damaging first; (2) whether 'thesis survives' overclaims given the null-control problem; (3) whether the p=1 -> p=2 repair is legitimate falsification practice or moving the goalposts; (4) VERDICT: ACCEPT / ACCEPT-WITH-AMENDMENTS (list them tersely) / REJECT.
